turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Ugh, sorry we're late, the elevator got stuck and he would not keep his coat on. Um, we're here because Leo's got a rash and a fever.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): You're fine, come on in. Hey Leo. Mom, just tell me the story in your own words, no rush.
[SEG0003] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Okay. Well, the fever came first. I thought it started Saturday, but actually I don't know, it might've been Friday night. He was hot and super cranky.
[SEG0004] person_3 (CAREGIVER): It was Friday. I had him after school Friday and he was warm, flushed warm, and just wiped out. Not Saturday.
[SEG0005] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right. Today's Wednesday, so that lands the fever at about four or five days, and we won't pin it tighter than that. When did the rash show up?
[SEG0006] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Sunday morning, for sure. Started on his face, then it, um, crept down his chest and his arms. Three days of spots.
[SEG0007] person_4 (PATIENT): Itchy.
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): Itchy spots. Leo, does your head hurt as well, or is it just the itch?
[SEG0009] person_4 (PATIENT): I don't know, doctor.
[SEG0010] person_3 (CAREGIVER): He's been sleeping on the couch instead of playing. And his eyes went pink yesterday.
[SEG0011] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Yeah, and he keeps scratching his belly. Dana stays with us on school nights, so she's seen more of this than I have.
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): Leo, have you been coughing at all?
[SEG0013] person_4 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0014] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Mm. Oh, his dinosaur backpack is still in the car, I'll grab it after. Sorry.
[SEG0015] person_2 (DOCTOR): What about his stomach. Any vomiting, or loose stools?
[SEG0016] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Umm. He didn't throw up. He had one loose stool this morning, I don't know if that even counts.
[SEG0017] person_2 (DOCTOR): And ears or throat, anything going on there?
[SEG0018] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Nothing. No ear pain, and he's been eating popsicles, no sore throat.
[SEG0019] person_2 (DOCTOR): Has he been on any medicine for this?

[SEG0020] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Children's tylenol. Err, a hundred and sixty milligrams, I almost said one-twenty but no, the bottle says 160. Every six hours for the fever, and I stopped it this morning cause I got scared the rash was from the medicine.
[SEG0021] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Oh, and my sister would not stop texting me to give him benedryl. We never gave it. Not once.
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any allergies I should know about, medicines or anything else?
[SEG0023] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No. Nothing he's reacted to.
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): Alright Leo, I'm going to take a look. You can stay on mom's lap. Temp here is 101.4, heart rate 128, oxygen sat 98 percent, and he's breathing about 22 times a minute.

[SEG0025] person_2 (DOCTOR): There's a red blotchy rash on his face, chest, and both arms. Eyes are a little bloodshot on both sides. Throat's mildly pink, no pus. I don't see any Koplik spots inside the cheeks. Lungs are clear.
[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): Honestly I was going to swab his throat for strep today and start amoxicilin, 400 milligrams twice a day. Scarlet fever was sitting on my list.
[SEG0027] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Oh. Um, before you do that. A kid in his class, Jordan, was out with the measles. That's why I panicked and came in. I don't know if Leo's shots cover it.
[SEG0028] person_3 (CAREGIVER): The school email said measles, yeah. Confirmed, not just a rumor. And the vaccine card, we couldn't find it. Mom thinks maybe he only had the baby shots.

[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): Okay. That changes things. Let me count it out. Classmate with measles, rash started Sunday, so if he was exposed about ten days before that, we're inside the seven to fourteen day window, and with the MMR up in the air I am not treating this as strep.

[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): So no antibiotic, and we'll skip the strep swab. What I want instead is a measles igm blood test. The nurse draws it Thursday morning at eight. He can eat a normal breakfast, no fasting.

[SEG0031] person_2 (DOCTOR): If that igm comes back borderline, then we do a PCR swab. Not before. And if the fever and the rash do not settle over the next few days, we might get a chest x-ray. I'm not ordering that now.

[SEG0032] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'll see you back here in one week either way, so we can go over those bloods. Keep him home, no school and no playdates, through Thursday, that's four days after the rash started. If he gets worse before the blood draw, call us, don't wait.

[SEG0033] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'll notify the health department today about a suspected case. My working read is possible measles, but it could still be some other viral rash. I can't lock it in until the bloods come back. Leo, you were brave.

spec.situation: Parents of a child with rash and fever after a classmate had measles; vaccination status vague; doctor examines, counts days, plans notification and isolation advice.

traps.happens: The doctor asks only two to four review-of-systems questions (for example fever, weight, cough). Several other body systems are never asked about. One of the asked questions gets a vague or mixed answer.
traps.label_rule: negative_findings / review_of_systems ONLY for items the doctor actually asked AND the patient answered, evidence = that question and answer. Never add review-of-systems entries for systems nobody asked about, and never cite an unrelated turn (for example a turn about tiredness) for a system review.

traps.happens: In the plan the doctor books some tests or visits for a definite time ('the nurse takes bloods Thursday morning', 'I'll see you in two weeks') and makes others conditional ('if those are borderline we do the third test', 'if it does not settle, a scan').
traps.label_rule: Booked or arranged = status planned. Only the hedged ones are conditional. Never mark a booked test conditional or 'if needed'. Instructions for the booked test (fasting, time, medicine timing) belong to that test's action, not a separate invented plan item.

features: doctor_changes_mind: the doctor says one plan, then changes it after new information; the label holds the final plan.

stopped_or_never_taken: a medicine the patient stopped, was never given or only took once ('I stopped it in March'). Status discontinued, not current; a medicine never taken is not recorded as a medication.

bad.reason: Fever and 4-5 days supported; certainty wrong because onset Friday vs Saturday was uncertain/disputed.
bad.text: Fever (category=constitutional, status=present, duration=approximately 4 to 5 days, onset=Friday night or Saturday, temporality=current, reported_by=family_member, certainty=certain)
